purpose: Compute and close baker's percentages, hydration/fat/sugar/leavening budgets, pan geometry, scaling laws, and bake-time priors so formulas are quantitative and reproducible.
assumptions: mass in grams is the native unit; volume inputs carry density assumptions
product-class bands are heuristic priors not laws of nature
no lab titration of acid or DSC of starch unless user supplies data
exclusions: clinical dietetics calculations for medical conditions

competency_questions.question: How is this formula expressed in baker's percentages and what is the flour base?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lists flour base membership and each ingredient as % flour in grams

competency_questions.question: What are the hydration, fat, sugar, and salt budgets as % flour?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: reports each budget with sources itemized for water and fat especially

competency_questions.question: Is total hydration closed including eggs, milk, and purees, and is it in band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: shows water fraction sum and product-class band comparison

competency_questions.question: What is true fat % accounting for butter water and chocolate cocoa butter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: butter counted as ~80-82% fat; inclusions' fat noted if material

competency_questions.question: What is the sugar budget including liquid sweetener solids and assembled components?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: liquid sweeteners split solids/water; layer assembly averages if multi-component

competency_questions.question: How should chemical leavener or yeast be dosed for this flour base and schedule?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives % flour, format conversions if needed, and tight tolerance on minors

competency_questions.question: How do you scale this formula to a new yield without breaking pans or budgets?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: uniform gram scale, pan revalidation, loss-aware portions

competency_questions.question: Given pan dimensions and batter mass, what depth and fill fraction result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: computes volume, fill fraction, and depth estimate

competency_questions.question: How should bake time priors change when depth or pan shape changes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: adjusts time prior from depth/composition and requires doneness checks

competency_questions.question: Does the formula pass full budget closure for its product class?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: checklist pass/waive per hydration fat sugar salt leaven mass pan

competency_questions.question: Given dietary constraints, can the product class survive after budget reclosure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: feasibility verdict and redesign or class change if needed

competency_questions.question: How are volumetric inputs converted and what uncertainty remains?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: density assumptions stated; flour variance acknowledged

glossary.definition: Ingredient mass divided by total flour mass × 100, with flour defined as 100%
Total water mass from all sources as % of flour base
The declared set of flours/powders that constitute the 100% denominator
Material fat, sugar, and dairy load that shifts a dough/batter out of lean-bread behavior
Batter or dough volume as a fraction of pan volumetric capacity before bake
Vertical thickness of raw mass in the pan; primary driver of center bake time
State where hydration, fat, sugar, salt, leavener, mass, and pan feasibility are all checked
Mass not reaching saleable portions due to adhesion, evaporation, or trim
Multiplier applied uniformly to all baker % gram quantities to change yield
Fat mass after adjusting butter, cream, egg yolk, and cocoa butter contributions as % flour

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for culinary_formulation_math work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Express every ingredient as percent of total flour mass (flour = 100%). Baker's percent makes formulas comparable across batch sizes and reveals hydration, fat, sugar, and salt bands independent of yield. Convert cups to grams before computing; volume is not a baker % input.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ingredient density table revision or flour blend changes the 100% baseline definition

pros.claim: Baker % normalizes formulas so a 70% hydration dough is meaningful at any batch size
pros.example: 500 g flour + 350 g water is 70% hydration whether or not eggs are present

cons.claim: Multi-flour blends require a defined total flour basis; purees are not flour
cons.example: 100 g AP + 50 g cocoa: decide if cocoa counts in flour base or as separate dry

failure_modes: computing % on total batter weight and calling it baker %
using cup measures as if they were mass
acceptance_tests: all ingredients listed in grams and as % of declared flour base

nodes.definition: Declare what counts as the flour 100% base: wheat flour only, or flour+cocoa+nut meal policy. Consistency of the base is mandatory for hydration and enrichment math. Changing the base mid-project invalidates all percentages.

included: single vs multi-component flour base policy
rebasing rules when dry substitutes enter

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: nut flour or cocoa added to dry base without rebasing percentages

pros.claim: Explicit flour-base policy prevents silent percent drift when cocoa or almond meal is added
pros.example: treat cocoa as separate dry at 10% of wheat flour, not as part of 100% base, for a devil's food

cons.claim: requires care at edges

failure_modes: skipping this unit degrades formula quality
acceptance_tests: flour base membership is explicitly listed
all baker % values use the same base definition
revisit_triggers: cross-team formula handoff with different base convention

nodes.definition: Set total water (including water fractions of eggs, milk, purees) as % of flour. Typical bands: stiff cookie doughs ~20-40% free liquid, cake batters ~60-100%+, lean bread 60-75%, high-hydration ciabatta 75-85%+. Band depends on flour protein and enrichment. Closing hydration means summing all water sources, not only the water line.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: wet ingredient substitution changes hidden water fraction

pros.claim: Closed hydration predicts dough feel and starch set window better than the water line alone
pros.example: eggs at 50 g on 250 g flour add ~15% hydration-equivalent water

cons.claim: requires care at edges

failure_modes: skipping this unit degrades formula quality
acceptance_tests: hydration includes itemized water fractions
product-class band cited
revisit_triggers: chronic slack or stiff dough relative to target

nodes.definition: Track total fat (butter water-adjusted, oil, egg yolk fat, cream fat, chocolate cocoa butter) as baker % of flour. Bands: lean bread <5%, enriched dough 10-50%+, pound cake ~50%+, shortbread very high. Fat budget predicts tenderness, spread, and emulsion difficulty.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: butter vs oil swap or chocolate addition changes true fat %

pros.claim: True fat % explains why European butter formulas differ from oil muffins at equal butter mass
pros.example: 100 g butter ≈ 81 g fat + 16 g water + solids on 250 g flour

cons.claim: Label 'butter' vs 'baking sticks' fat fraction can differ slightly by brand

failure_modes: counting butter mass as 100% fat in hydration and fat budgets
adding chocolate without cocoa-butter fat line
acceptance_tests: fat budget itemizes sources and reports total fat % flour

nodes.definition: Sum sucrose, brown sugar (as mass), honey/syrups (as solids + water split), and chocolate sugar into baker % sugar. Bands: bread 0-10%, enriched 10-25%, cookies 30-80%+, high-ratio cakes ~100% sugar on flour. Sugar budget couples to hydration (hygroscopy) and bake time (browning/set delay).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: liquid sweetener swap changes solids vs water split

pros.claim: Sugar % band is a product-class fingerprint useful for reverse-engineering recipes
pros.example: ~50-70% sugar cookies vs ~100% sugar high-ratio layer cakes

cons.claim: Polyols and rare sugars do not map 1:1 to sucrose bulk or browning

failure_modes: treating honey grams as pure sugar solids
sugar-free claim without bulk rebuild plan
acceptance_tests: sugar budget lists sources with solids fraction for liquids

nodes.definition: Salt as baker % of flour: bread ~1.8-2.2%, enriched sweet doughs often 1.2-1.8%, cookies variable. Convert crystal types by mass not volume. Salt budget is small but high leverage on gluten and fermentation rate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: kosher vs table salt density confusion or low-sodium request

pros.claim: Weighed salt keeps rheology stable across crystal brands
pros.example: 2.0% salt on flour regardless of flake size

cons.claim: Low-sodium reformulation needs flavor rebuild beyond % cut
cons.example: simply halving salt tastes flat without acid/umami compensation

failure_modes: tablespoon scaling when batch doubles
forgetting salt in preferment and final dough double-salting
acceptance_tests: salt % by mass in band for product class

nodes.definition: Dose baking powder/soda as baker % of flour and against acid load. Heuristic bands: baking powder ~1-5% of flour depending on product; soda paired to acid milliequivalents when known. Scale leavener with flour, not with eggs alone. At altitude, reduce dose.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: altitude change or acid ingredient change invalidates prior dose

pros.claim: Flour-relative dosing prevents runaway gas when batch size changes
pros.example: same 3% powder on flour at 200 g or 2 kg flour

cons.claim: requires care at edges

failure_modes: skipping this unit degrades formula quality
acceptance_tests: leavener % of flour recorded
altitude note if elevation material

nodes.definition: Yeast mass as % flour interacts with dough temperature and ferment time. Instant yeast ~0.5-1.5% for direct doughs; preferments use less commercial yeast. Conversion: instant ≈ active dry × 0.75; fresh ≈ instant × 3. Time-temperature substitutes for mass within limits.

excluded: wild capture starter microbiology lab methods

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: yeast format change or proof box temperature process change

pros.claim: Trading lower yeast for longer cool ferment improves flavor at controlled schedule
pros.example: 0.2% yeast overnight cold bulk vs 1% same-day

cons.claim: Too little yeast with cold dough and short schedule underproofs
cons.example: fridge dough pulled early looks dense

failure_modes: applying bread yeast % to sweet dough without time increase
confusing instant and active dry 1:1
acceptance_tests: yeast type, % flour, target dough temp, and endpoint criterion listed

nodes.definition: Sum all ingredient grams to total formula mass; yield is total mass minus process loss (mixing bowl left-back, bake evaporation, trim). Predicted baked yield needs an evaporation factor by product class (cookies lower loss %, lean bread higher crust loss).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaporation factor revised from weigh-before/after bake data

pros.claim: Mass balance catches missing ingredients and predicts pan fill
pros.example: sum to 1200 g batter; 10 pans × 100 g + 200 g reserve

cons.claim: Evaporation factors are product- and oven-specific priors

failure_modes: assuming baked weight equals raw weight
forgetting inclusions added after % calculation
acceptance_tests: total mass and expected baked yield with stated loss factor
revisit_triggers: new oven or pan changes loss

nodes.definition: Pan volume (L×W×H for rectangular; πr²h for round) and batter fill fraction determine depth. Surface-to-volume ratio drives browning and bake time. Bundt vs sheet pan at equal mass bake very differently. Always match formula mass to pan volume capacity (~50-67% fill typical for cakes to allow rise).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pan brand dimensions differ from nominal size labels

pros.claim: Matching batter mass to pan volume prevents overflow and collapsed underfill
pros.example: 8-inch round ~6 cup capacity; fill ~1/2 to 2/3 with layer-cake batter

cons.claim: requires care at edges

failure_modes: skipping this unit degrades formula quality
acceptance_tests: pan volume and fill fraction stated
batter mass matches capacity band

nodes.definition: Depth (cm) of batter or dough in the pan controls heat path to the center. Deeper masses need lower temperature and longer time; thin sheet cakes finish fast. Depth is the bridge from pan geometry and mass to bake-time models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: same mass loaded into different footprint pan changes depth

pros.claim: Depth predicts why a cupcake and a 9x13 of the same batter need different times
pros.example: 3 cm sheet vs 6 cm loaf center lag

cons.claim: requires care at edges

failure_modes: skipping this unit degrades formula quality
acceptance_tests: depth or fill height estimated before bake-time set

nodes.definition: Scale all ingredients by the same factor on flour base to change yield. Do not scale pan count without checking depth. Yeast and chemical leaveners generally scale with flour; spices and salt scale with flour but taste-check at extremes. Mixing time does not scale linearly with mass — dough development is energy and geometry dependent.

included: what not to scale linearly (mix time, bake time)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scale factor >3× or equipment change (home mixer to spiral)

pros.claim: Flour-base scaling keeps all budgets invariant when only yield changes
pros.example: 2× flour and 2× every ingredient preserves 65% hydration

cons.claim: 10× home recipes can fail from mixer underpower and different heat transfer
cons.example: double batch in same pan is a depth change not a pure scale

failure_modes: scaling bake time by the same factor as mass
scaling eggs by count rounding error without gram correction
acceptance_tests: scaled formula remains in baker % identity with original
pan and bake plan revisited after scale

nodes.definition: Heuristic: bake time rises faster than linear with depth; a common prior is time ratio roughly scales with depth^1.2–1.5 for similar batter and oven, then confirm with internal temperature. Higher sugar/fat delays set. Convection vs still air changes effective time. Never publish a time without a doneness signal hierarchy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven type change or sugar/fat budget shift invalidates prior time curve

pros.claim: Depth-aware time priors reduce raw centers when pans change
pros.example: moving from cupcakes to 8-inch layers multiplies time more than mass ratio alone suggests

cons.claim: requires care at edges

failure_modes: skipping this unit degrades formula quality
acceptance_tests: bake plan includes depth, time prior, and non-time doneness checks
revisit_triggers: raw center or overbake edge failures

nodes.definition: Close the formula: hydration, fat, sugar, salt, leavener within product-class bands; total mass equals sum of parts; pan fill and depth feasible; scale factor consistent. Open budgets (unknown water in a mystery puree) must be flagged before bake advice locks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any single budget line edited without re-running full closure

pros.claim: Full closure catches incompatible targets (e.g., 40% hydration pound cake)
pros.example: checklist fails until water sources added for cake band

cons.claim: Bands are priors; regional styles may sit outside house bands intentionally

failure_modes: locking a bake schedule with an open hydration line
closing mass but not pan fill
acceptance_tests: closure checklist completed with pass/waive per budget line
pan mass and depth feasible

nodes.definition: Convert cups/spoons to grams with ingredient-specific densities (flour sifted vs spooned differs ~20%+). Prefer weighing. When only volume given, state density assumptions and uncertainty. Flour is the highest-variance common conversion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: density table update or flour brand packing behavior change

pros.claim: Stating conversion assumptions makes volumetric recipes debuggable
pros.example: AP flour 120 g/cup spooned vs 140 g/cup scooped — pick one and declare

cons.claim: Internet density tables disagree; variance remains

failure_modes: mixing density sources mid-formula
treating 1 cup all ingredients as 240 g
acceptance_tests: volume inputs converted with named density assumptions

nodes.definition: Encode allergies, vegan, sugar-reduction, and gluten-free as hard constraints on allowed ingredients, then reclose budgets. Constraints are not flavor notes — they remove mass that must be replaced on functional axes. Multi-constraint sets may be infeasible at original product class.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new hard constraint added after first closure

pros.claim: Treating vegan+GF+sugar-free as simultaneous hard constraints surfaces infeasibility early
pros.example: angel food cannot keep identity under all three without becoming a different dessert

cons.claim: Users may reject product-class change even when math requires it
cons.example: insisting on identical pound cake texture egg-free and fat-free

failure_modes: applying constraints only to shopping list not to structure math
silent drop of salt for 'healthy' without flavor plan
acceptance_tests: constraints listed as hard/soft
if infeasible, alternative product class proposed

nodes.definition: For multi-component products (cake + filling + frosting, laminated dough layers), budget each component separately then assemble mass ratios (e.g., frosting : cake crumb 0.3–0.6). Assembled product hydration and sweetness are weighted averages of components.

excluded: wedding cake structural engineering beyond mass ratios

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: filling type change alters assembled sugar/fat averages

pros.claim: Separate component budgets prevent frosting sugar from polluting cake flour % math
pros.example: cake at 100% sugar on flour; frosting budgeted per gram of cake

cons.claim: User-facing slices care about assembled sweetness not component baker %
cons.example: a low-sugar cake with heavy ganache still tastes sweet

failure_modes: mixing frosting sugar into cake flour base percentages
ignoring soak syrup as a water+sugar addition
acceptance_tests: each component closed; assembly ratios stated

nodes.definition: Classify doughs/batters as lean vs enriched by fat+sugar+dairy thresholds (e.g., brioche enrichment when butter >20% flour and eggs present). Enrichment changes expected hydration feel, yeast dose, and mix method. Misclassification applies wrong bands.

excluded: legal standards of identity for enriched flour fortification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: added butter or sugar pushes formula across enrichment threshold

pros.claim: Classifying enrichment selects the correct hydration and yeast priors
pros.example: brioche at 50% butter uses different mix and ferment than baguette at 2% fat

cons.claim: Borderline formulas (10% butter sandwich bread) sit between heuristics

failure_modes: applying lean bread hydration feel targets to panettone
using muffin method priors for laminated dough
acceptance_tests: enrichment class labeled with fat+sugar evidence
revisit_triggers: fat or sugar budget crosses threshold

nodes.definition: Account for mix bowl adhesion, divider waste, bake evaporation, and post-bake trim. Use product-class factors as priors (e.g., 8-15% bake mass loss for many breads; less for high-fat cookies). Yield math without loss overpromises portions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: weigh-before/after data updates loss factor

pros.claim: Loss-aware yield prevents shorting a party tray of 24 cookies
pros.example: plan 10% extra dough mass for scoop loss and spread trim

cons.claim: Over-applying bread evaporation factors to brownies overproduces
cons.example: high-fat dense products lose less moisture

failure_modes: quoting raw batter portions as finished servings
ignoring soak-up of syrups that add mass after bake
acceptance_tests: loss factor stated by category for yield claims

nodes.definition: Define acceptable variance: home scale ±1-2 g on minor ingredients, tighter on leavener and salt relative to their small masses. Rounding eggs to whole units requires gram compensation with water or omitting elsewhere. Tolerance bands prevent false precision theater while protecting high-leverage minors.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scale precision class changes (0.1 g vs 1 g home scale)

pros.claim: Tighter absolute tolerance on 5 g soda than on 200 g flour matches leverage
pros.example: ±0.5 g on soda vs ±5 g on flour

cons.claim: Obsessive 0.01 g precision on flour does not improve home cakes

failure_modes: rounding 1.5 eggs to 2 without removing ~25 g elsewhere
measuring soda by volume loosely
acceptance_tests: tolerance policy stated for flour, water, minors

nodes.definition: Optional overlay: unit costs × grams for batch cost and cost per baked portion after loss. Cost never overrides food-safety or structure closure. Used when user asks for cheaper swaps — still reclose functional budgets after cheaper ingredient substitution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ingredient unit prices change or cheaper substitute proposed

pros.claim: Portion cost after loss gives honest catering quotes
pros.example: raw dough cost / (count × (1-loss))

cons.claim: Cheapest fat may be rancid risk or wrong plastic range

failure_modes: optimizing cost before structure closure
ignoring loss in per-serving cost
acceptance_tests: if cost used, structure budgets still closed first

nodes.definition: Chocolate chips, nuts, fruit, and seeds are often budgeted as % flour on top of base formula (e.g., 20-40% chips). They add mass and local heat sinks but usually are outside hydration flour base. Fold-in timing does not change mass math but changes distribution.

included: wet vs dry fruit water accounting

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: inclusion type change (dried vs wet fruit) alters water and sugar

pros.claim: Budgeting inclusions separately keeps base crumb math clean
pros.example: cookie dough base closed, then +30% chips on flour

cons.claim: Wet fruit bleeds water and sugar into base during bake
cons.example: blueberry muffins need base adjustment or coated fruit

failure_modes: dumping inclusions into flour base % and wrecking hydration interpretation
scaling chips with pan size only ignoring flour base
acceptance_tests: inclusion % and wet/dry class recorded

conflict_axes.name: precision_vs_practicality
conflict_axes.description: Lab-grade gram precision vs home cooking speed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weigh high-leverage minors; allow coarser flour tolerance

conflict_axes.name: mass_scale_vs_bake_time_scale
conflict_axes.description: Users scale time with mass factor incorrectly

conflict_axes.name: band_purity_vs_regional_style
conflict_axes.description: House bands vs legitimate style outliers

conflict_axes.name: component_math_vs_assembled_taste
conflict_axes.description: Baker % per layer vs eaten slice sweetness/fat
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: report both component budgets and weighted assembly

conflict_axes.name: constraint_fidelity_vs_product_identity
conflict_axes.description: Hard diet constraints vs keeping original product class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state infeasibility; propose nearest feasible class

conflict_axes.name: single_pan_deep_vs_multi_pan_shallow
conflict_axes.description: One deep pan convenience vs even bake
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer depth in band for product; split pans if needed

conflict_axes.name: yeast_mass_vs_schedule
conflict_axes.description: More yeast for speed vs flavor from time

conflict_axes.name: inclusion_load_vs_base_structure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap inclusions % flour; adjust bake for heat sinks

edge_cases.description: Only volumetric recipe available with packed brown sugar and scooped flour
edge_cases.trigger: cups-only input with high flour variance risk
edge_cases.mitigation: declare density assumptions; widen uncertainty; recommend scale for next iteration

edge_cases.description: Double batch left in a single original pan
edge_cases.mitigation: treat as depth change; lower temp extend time; or split pans
reduce chemical leavener slightly; increase liquid; adjust temp/time; trial

edge_cases.description: Butter measured as fat 100% in spreadsheet
edge_cases.mitigation: apply ~81% fat / ~16% water split for butter; reclose

edge_cases.description: Honey swapped 1:1 for sucrose by grams
edge_cases.mitigation: count ~80% sugar solids ~17% water; reduce other liquid; reclose

edge_cases.description: Vegan + gluten-free + deep sugar cut on angel food
edge_cases.trigger: multi hard constraints on foam cake identity
edge_cases.mitigation: declare infeasible identity; propose different dessert class
water-fill measure pan volume; set fill fraction; then depth estimate

edge_cases.trigger: yield planned on raw mass only
edge_cases.mitigation: apply loss factor and bake a buffer tray

edge_cases.description: Mixer cannot develop double dough mass
edge_cases.mitigation: split batches; do not fake scale in one underpowered mix
recompute depth; cut time drastically; watch doneness signals
coat fruit, reduce other liquid slightly, fold late; accept some bleed

workflow.description: Convert all volume inputs to grams with declared densities
List what is in the 100% flour base
Set chemical or yeast dose from flour base and schedule
Label lean vs enriched and select band set
Total mass and process loss yield estimate
workflow.gate: total mass equals sum of parts

workflow.description: Choose pans; compute fill and depth
Depth- and composition-aware time prior with doneness checks

workflow.gate: all lines pass or waived with reason

workflow.description: Apply diet constraints and optional cost overlay
workflow.gate: structure still closed after any swap

priority_rationale: Baker % and flour base unlock all budgets; mass and pan geometry unlock depth and time; closure and constraints finish the formula before cost overlays.

dominance_rules.action: reclose budgets after any cheaper swap

dominance_rules.trigger: user scales time by mass factor

dominance_rules.rationale: infeasible identity should be renamed not faked

dominance_rules.action: require grams for salt and leavener

dominance_rules.rationale: overflow and raw centers are failures

dominance_rules.action: apply process loss before promising counts

anti_rework_rules.prevents: raw deep centers or burnt thin trays
gummy fruit zones and wrong hydration

iteration_protocol.action: reduce depth or temp; extend time; recheck sugar/fat delay
recompute hidden water; verify flour base
check mixer energy, pan depth, loss factors
move flour and minors to weighed grams
